prior_reason_rebuttal: Prior verdict called this 'Aesthetics training institute/school — not a patient-facing clinic'. That is true of most of the site (advanced-aesthetic-courses, injectable-courses, laser-courses, bundle-courses are all tuition-priced certification courses for aestheticians/medical professionals), and /model-services/ is a free-but-discounted 'apply to become a model' program where students under supervision practice on volunteers -- the classic model-call pattern the brief says not to decide alone. But the site also has a distinct, genuinely public-facing page, /treatment-services/, explicitly describing treatments 'performed by certified/licensed professionals' (not students) at published per-treatment prices (Laser Hair Removal from $20, RF Skin Tightening $120, Chemical Peel $150, Microneedling $150, IPL $200, etc.), booked 'by appointment ONLY' via phone/email -- and /model-services/ itself explicitly distinguishes this from the model program: 'We also offer scheduled treatment services that are open to the public... please visit our services page.' Because there is a real patient-facing, publicly-bookable treatment menu independent of the training/model activity, this clears the bar in rule 5 for INCLUDE rather than AMBIGUOUS_ACADEMY.
